How 'in-the-wrong' would it be if I were to pentest scammer websites?

in my book, if the scammer came to you rather than you going looking for them, you're not in the wrong at all. I've been doing exactly that with spammers since the late 90s, it's in our T&C that all commercial users consent to a full pentest with the results to be published on a forum of our choice unless prior authorization is gained, and those T&C are in the mailserver headers so the spammer's mail software gets a copy of them with every connection (not my fault if the spammr doesn't read everything in the server handshake).

On the legal side, you put yourself at risk by touching infrastructure that does not belong to you, or that which you are not specifically authorized to touch. That's the hard and fast of that.

Ethically, I don't think it'd be very wrong. It's kind of like robbing a drug dealer in a way. However, my moral compass and society's are hardly aligned 100%.

Legally? Very, you are still interfering with someone else's systems, and could likely be prosecuted under the CFAA (assuming USA), especially if you consider that the scammers likely don't own the servers they are using, and instead are renting them from (semi) legitimate hosting providers.

Morally? Go right ahead, do your best to fuck up their operations. Be careful, though, you don't want to accidentally taint an ongoing investigation and implicate yourself for shit you didn't do by, say, gaining root access to a box, using that root FTPing into it, and having your traffic show up in a log that later ends up in the hands of law enforcement. That would lead to awkward questions, no matter the situation.

I would avoid it. If you want practice, try hackthissite, if its not too basic for you, otherwise, vulnhub has some VM images to practice on. If you feel like you are truly ready for real world, there are freelance pentest sites (think rentacoder for pentesters). They don't pay well, but they DO pad a resume, and the DO actually pay, and they get you exploiting actual sites, with the written permission of the site owner, of course.

If your end goal is to cause grief for the scammers, I highly recommend simply doing your own investigative work, tipping off law enforcement with juicy personal details and evidence, and watching the fireworks, much like Brian Krebs does on his blog for the "breadcrumbs" articles

Edit: To be clear with CYA. I am not condoning or recommending any illegal action such as was suggested in title. I understand and appreciate that it is VERY illegal, and would never suggest someone do it, I am merely pointing out that, despite the legal stance on it, I personally find no moral qualm with it, an opinion which I am free to hold.
